integrations.name: Looong Hook
integrations.summary: A canonical LOOONG/WETH pool where verified buys create non-transferable custodied positions, mature holders can earn WETH rewards after 30 days, and part of the sell fee can move from early profitable exits to eligible holders.

integration.standardSwapBehavior: Source tests cover ordinary exact-input and exact-output swaps in both directions with empty hookData through LooongRouter. Verified position buys and sells use one-shot authenticated intents through that router; an optional exact-output witness uses a separate versioned domain. Compatibility with Hookr's production router path is not yet proven.

dedicatedRouter.purpose: Required for position-creating buys and owner-bound sells from hook custody. Ordinary swaps can use empty hookData without creating or consuming a position.

security.authorityModel: PoolManager, registrar, trusted router, tokens, fee beneficiary, fee rates, and maturity are immutable. The one-shot launcher exposes no ownership, upgrade, liquidity-removal, fee-collection, rescue, or arbitrary-call path; the immutable fee beneficiary can claim the base-fee liability.
knownRisks: The repository labels itself a reference implementation that is unaudited and not ready for public deployment.

Before another owner has mature shares, a verified seller can receive the full 2.90% sell component back and effectively pay only the 0.10% base hook fee; the advertised anti-flip pressure is therefore weak during bootstrap.
Verified buys place LOOONG in hook custody and rely on internal non-transferable position, basis, rebate, and reward accounting.
Free withdrawal and alternate pools can bypass the position-and-reward behavior, while separate wallets can sybil mature-holder eligibility.
Before- and after-swap return deltas, exact-output gross-up, partial-fill handling, and PoolManager claim conservation require independent review and target-chain fork testing.
The holder-incentive outcome depends on early-profit, maturity, wallet-sybil, ordinary-swap, and MEV behavior; source tests are not a production economic review.
No public deployment, initialized pool, locked-liquidity receipt, source verification, or live monitoring evidence has been supplied.

integrations.name: Lucky Hook
integrations.summary: An ownerless canonical ETH/LUCK pool that takes hook-level swap fees, funds Chainlink VRF, and distributes periodic rewards to eligible mature buyers.

integration.standardSwapBehavior: Empty hookData is accepted and non-empty hookData reverts. Delta-return fee accounting changes swap settlement, so the pool is not vanilla even though ordinary swaps do not require custom hook data.

dedicatedRouter.purpose: The repository's authenticated payer and recipient settlement surface for the canonical product flow.

security.authorityModel: The source describes an ownerless hook with immutable token, PoolManager, VRF wrapper, registrar, and reward parameters.
knownRisks: The repository states that it has not been audited.
Reward liveness depends on Chainlink VRF funding, fulfillment, and timeout recovery.
Fee, liability, buyer-index, and random-selection invariants require independent production review.

integrations.name: Wager Hook
integrations.summary: An immutable canonical ETH/WAGER pool where ordinary swaps use empty hook data, exact-input swaps may optionally create fixed-odds WETH wager tickets, and randomness is requested only after the season closes for later settlement.

integration.standardSwapBehavior: Empty hookData remains an ordinary swap. The optional wager path uses exact 36-byte versioned hookData and the dedicated router; routed Uniswap trades can use the ordinary path without enabling the wager feature.

dedicatedRouter.purpose: Required only for the optional wager flow that binds a WETH stake to executed swap volume.

dependencies.name: Production randomness provider
dependencies.notes: No target-chain provider has been evidenced for Robinhood Chain. The integration remains blocked until the provider and trust model are selected and reviewed.

security.authorityModel: The source describes no mutable administrator, pause, upgrade, rescue, odds-change, or dependency-replacement path after launch.
knownRisks: The repository states that it is unaudited and not ready for real-value deployment.
The Robinhood Chain path has no evidenced production randomness provider; changing away from Chainlink VRF requires a new dependency and trust-model review.
Wager solvency and settlement depend on reserve accounting and the selected randomness provider's lifecycle behavior.
